rationale: itnet_v2-claude-agentic: itnet_k=1, unet_c=16, itnet_alpha_init=0.0026, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=0.00025, pretrain_epochs=15, pretrain_patience=15, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=600, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=ITER-2 (breast itnet_v2 search-20260703-01, strict 20-min budget). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 = val_ssim 0.7636 / hr 0.0000 / PSNR 23.73 vs baseline_PSNR 36.32 / RMSE 0.02222 / alpha_learned 0.002597, elapsed 240s (well inside 1200s budget); pretrain loss fell to ~1e-6 by epoch 3 (denoiser converged). (2) FAILURE MODE: the recon is FAR WORSE than the FBP baseline (PSNR 23.73 << 36.32, hr=0). Pretrain learned a near-perfect (FBP->truth) map, but the k=4 data-consistency loop DESTROYS it: dc_step does x <- x - alpha*FBP(R*x - g) using a FILTERED backprojection of the sino residual; on breast's 128-view SPARSE geometry with high dynamic range (display_max=0.5, ~10x Mayo's 0.05), each of the 4 DC steps injects sparse-view streak artifacts that overwhelm the denoised image. The denoiser alone would nearly match FBP; the repeated DC application is the corruptor. (3) ONE KNOB: itnet_k 4 -> 1 (minimal single DC step). ALL else identical to iter-1 (unet_c=16, alpha_init=0.0026, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=2.5e-4, pretrain_epochs=15, patience=15, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=600, val_n=200, seed=42). (4) HYPOTHESIS: if I cut itnet_k 4->1, val hr rises above 0 (recon approaches the pretrained-denoiser quality, PSNR toward the ~36 baseline band) because a single mild DC step corrupts far less than four compounding sparse-view backprojection steps -- confirming DC-over-application as the iter-1 failure. FALSIFIER: if hr stays 0 at k=1, the single DC step ITSELF (its FBP-of-residual formulation) is the corruptor regardless of count, and iter-3 must instead attack alpha (lower itnet_alpha_init) or the DC formulation. (5) BUDGET: k=1 is CHEAPER than k=4 at both train (DC in-loop) and val; iter-1 used 240s at k=4, so k=1 is comfortably < 1200s. (6) Loop continues; I dispatch iter-3 myself when iter-2 lands.
